title: Tell new hires the truth
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who do you tell the truth to before they join you?
Jose said the person in the book meets a designer who vibes with him: cool, collected, with self-confidence and polite humility. There are certain people who can vibe with him a little more.

Then he hires his right-hand person, Jose said, a clay modeler and engineer. He tells him the truth: this is a garage van, and we may go bankrupt. But he says if he is hardcore about building rockets, this is easier than rockets. And the man says: I'm all in.
Jose said that a man who had thrived in the battery work made a statement about the boss, and read it.
True industrial design must connect the looks of a product to its engineering.
He said it is groundbreaking when aesthetics and engineering are combined. A student had also thought it funny that the person had first hired a designer for the design and then went another way.
What would you tell a new hire about what they are walking into?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you would tell a new hire about the risks.
Write what would make a person say: I'm all in.
Write how the look of your product connects to how it works.
Write who in your team vibes with you and who challenges you.
Write what you would say if the job might fail.

check.q: What did the person in the book tell the engineer he hired?
choices: That it was a garage van and they may go bankrupt

check.q: What must industrial design connect, according to the line Jose read?
choices: The looks of a product to its engineering

recap: Tell new hires the truth. Connect the look to the engineering.
